verdict.headline: Iran's new Hormuz demands stall oil deal and lift crude as equity markets hold record highs
verdict.label: HOLD — 1 of 6 breached: 30Y ~5.08%; Sept hike ~44% (Kalshi, from 67% pre-NFP); ESU26 +0.3% at ~7,782; WTI $78.72 just $0.28 from $79 trigger; Brent $84.39 just $0.61 from $85 trigger; Wednesday July CPI (Aug 12, 8:30 ET) is the week's resolving binary
verdict.rationale_short: The framework holds at 1 of 6 breached (30Y ~5.08%) but the oil indicators are back at near-trigger levels heading into the week. Friday's July NFP shock (-23K vs +83K consensus) drove the S&P 500 to a fresh record close of 7,757.64 (+0.62%) and compressed September hike odds from ~67% to ~44% (Kalshi). Monday premarket extends the equity calm: ESU26 +0.32% at ~7,782, NQ futures +0.58% at ~29,896. But oil is the new pressure point: over the weekend Iran's FM Araghchi clarified that a deal with Oman alone will NOT reopen the Strait of Hormuz — Iran requires the US to end the war and provide financial compensation, conditions outside the Oman-brokered framework. Houthi militants also claimed an attack on a Saudi refinery over the weekend. Result: WTI bounced to $78.72 (+0.69%), only $0.28 below the $79 formal trigger; Brent at $84.39 (+1.0%) is $0.61 below the $85 trigger. A single session oil spike on any Hormuz escalation activates a second regime breach (2-of-6), the most material scenario for the framework before Wednesday. BTC holds at $64,998 (Crypto.com live, 11:02 UTC Aug 10), Gate 2 buffer $2,998 above the $62,000 trigger. DXY at 99.5 has broken below the psychologically significant 100 handle on the NFP-driven rate unwind, a moderate macro tailwind for risk assets. Wednesday's July CPI is the singular binary: June came in at +2.9% YoY headline, +3.2% core. A July print at or below those levels pushes September hike odds toward 20%, may pull the 30Y below 5.00% (clearing the sole breach), and targets SPX above 7,850. A hot print re-escalates hike odds toward 65%+, deepens the 30Y breach, and turns Friday's record into an air pocket heading into the Aug 20 SPCX tranche unlock.

trade_setups.asset: July CPI — Wednesday August 12, 8:30 AM ET
trade_setups.thesis: Friday's NFP miss reset the rate-hike debate, making Wednesday's July CPI the week's singular binary. June came in at +2.9% YoY headline, +3.2% core. A July print at or below those levels pushes September hike odds from ~44% toward 20% — the de facto 'hold through year-end' signal that extends SPX records toward 7,850+ and may pull the 30Y below 5.00%, delivering 0-of-6 for the first time since May. A hot print (+3.2%+ headline or +3.5%+ core) re-escalates September odds toward 65%+, pushes the 30Y above 5.20%, and turns Friday's record close into an air pocket heading into the Aug 20 SPCX tranche unlock.
trade_setups.entry: Hold into Wednesday. Pre-CPI tells: 30Y yield action Tuesday (currently ~5.08%); a drift above 5.15% before the print signals bond markets pre-pricing a hot read. DXY at 99.5 is the secondary lead — a move above 100.50 post-CPI confirms rate re-escalation.
trade_setups.invalidation: CPI in-line (within ±0.1% of June levels) leaves September unresolved and the framework at 1-of-6 through the Aug 27 Jackson Hole keynote (Warsh) — base case extends without directional resolution.
trade_setups.horizon: 2 days (through July CPI, Wednesday August 12, 8:30 AM ET)

bear_case: A hot July CPI print Wednesday (Aug 12) is the primary risk: headline +3.2%+ or core +3.5%+ re-escalates September hike odds from ~44% toward 65%+ in a single session, pushes the 30Y above 5.20% (deepening the sole breach), and turns Friday's record SPX close at 7,757 into an air pocket heading into the Aug 20 SPCX tranche unlock. The more proximate risk is an oil spike: WTI at $78.72 is $0.28 from the $79 trigger and Brent at $84.39 is $0.61 from the $85 trigger — Iran's weekend clarification that a deal alone will not reopen the Strait of Hormuz (requiring US war termination and financial compensation) eliminates the near-term de-escalation scenario. A single Hormuz incident activates a second regime breach (2-of-6), combining rate risk and oil risk simultaneously heading into Wednesday's CPI. The tertiary risk remains the July NFP signal: 921,000 July temporary layoffs and prior-month revisions of -103K combined could signal a cycle turn rather than a one-off miss — if August employment confirms the July print, Q3 earnings revisions follow and the SPX record at 7,757 becomes the peak. If SPX loses the 7,600 level on a daily close before Wednesday's CPI, the hold thesis does not extend.
